inputs_used: content-system/personas/*.yaml (weights: planner_couple 0.40, funding_parent 0.20, uhnw 0.20, sceptic 0.10, search_visitor 0.10)

must_fix.issue: Mid-page Advisor line in the destination section reads as a generic end-to-end ad break with no tie to the section (planner), raises 'payments' commission questions (sceptic) and shows no proof for large weekends (uhnw).
must_fix.fix: E1: open the line on the multi-event weekend the section covers; brand-facts claims only. Fee/commission and scale questions are not answerable in this post (see conflicts_resolved and open_questions).

must_fix.issue: 'Split the list between families' leaves helpers with no way to get answers back to the couple, and assumes every family chases replies itself.
must_fix.fix: E2: ask each helper to pass every answer back so the one guest list stays accurate. E9 adds 'a family assistant' in the FAQ.

must_fix.issue: Light text 'your RSVP is the last piece of our puzzle' reads try-hard.
must_fix.fix: E3: 'are you in?' keeps the light tone. Planner's 'we would love to know if you are in' rejected as an echo of a removed competitor phrase.

should_fix.issue: Closing opener 'the real planning begins' is a brochure line and implies stays are sorted only after replies.
should_fix.fix: E4: 'the details firm up' (primary persona's wording).

should_fix.issue: Light email 'we will stop politely nagging' is the most eager line for older and private guests.
should_fix.fix: E5: 'we will set a place for you'.

should_fix.issue: Privacy Act paragraph feels heavy for readers who only want wording.
should_fix.fix: No edit. Paragraph stays as written (sourced, dated, not-legal-advice framing earned the sceptic's trust and covers a legality point). See conflicts_resolved.

should_fix.issue: Readers asked whether Wonderland Studio can be shared by several family members and whether it costs anything.
should_fix.fix: No copy change: Studio stays 'our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs' only. Sharing, cost and data storage go to the owner as an open question, not into this post.

consider.issue: Privacy advice stops short of helpers, where lists leak.
consider.fix: E6: ask helpers not to forward or screenshot the list.

consider.issue: Destination reminder does not ask about mobility or access needs before guests book travel.
consider.fix: E7: add one line asking for dietary, mobility or access needs.

consider.issue: 'Nothing sours goodwill faster' is an unsupported superlative.
FAQ assumes only parents or siblings help.
Key takeaways omit the reminder count.
consider.fix: E10: fold 'three reminders at most' into takeaway 4. A 5th takeaway is rejected (exactly 4 required).

consider.issue: Heading 'The number of reminders to send' does not match how people search.
consider.fix: Rejected: 'How many RSVP reminders to send' would be a question heading outside the FAQ. The FAQ already answers 'How frequently should you remind guests to RSVP?'.

consider.issue: Reader wants a ballpark of how long before the reply date to send the first reminder.
consider.fix: Rejected: no day or week counts by brief; the process guide link owns deadlines.

consider.issue: Primary CTA appears before any wording.
consider.fix: No move. Low severity from a 0.1-weight reader who called it low priority; the primary persona did not object and it is the only Concierge line a skimming destination couple sees before the wording. Link, anchor and position unchanged.

consider.issue: Parent wants to know the Advisor's name and to speak to a real person by phone; asks about after-hours support and deposit protection.
consider.fix: Not for this post: named person, phone line and on-the-ground claims are outside brand-facts. Concierge page question.

keep: Two-sentence direct answer in the intro (reminder before, personal follow-up after, last call only if a name is still blank).
Destination paragraph naming flights, leave, rooms and per-event headcounts.
Takeaway 'Match the channel to the guest' and the advice to call older relatives and check overseas time zones.
Per-event replies and the multi-event reminder wording ('A guest may come to the ceremony and dinner but arrive too late for welcome drinks').
'Three steps at most' and 'A guest who has ignored three kind notes is better reached by a call from someone they know.'
No-group-message privacy advice with the OAIC citation, and the dated Privacy Act paragraph (sceptic trust).
QR code advice with the ACSC citation and printing the web address beside it.
The rewritten call script (funding parent will print it).
Formal option leading every tone set.
The honest count-or-not trade-off in 'Deciding whether to count a guest'.
Closing line: single point of contact, quotes in AUD, inclusions confirmed in writing before you commit (most reassuring line for planner, parent and sceptic).
Access needs ask in the formal email.
conflicts_resolved: Privacy Act paragraph: planner_couple and search_visitor found it heavy; sceptic and funding_parent trusted it. Kept unchanged: the brief requires the privacy section, it is sourced and dated, and the primary persona called it accurate (only 'skipped it', low severity). Search visitor's 'In short,' prefix adds nothing.

Light tone: planner wants it toned down, uhnw and funding_parent want no more playful lines but accept it because formal leads. Light versions kept for all channels (brief requires three tones), with the two most eager lines softened (E3, E5).

Advisor 'payments': sceptic reads it as a possible commission; funding_parent sees it as accountability. Kept, because it is a brand-facts claim and the 0.4 + 0.2 weighted primary and parent readers value it. Fee and commission answers belong on /wonderland-concierge, never in this post.
UHNW proof of scale, exclusive use, security and private enquiry channel: out of scope for a DIY how-to and outside 'Claims we can make'. UHNW is a secondary reader here; no copy added.
Planner's light-text wording 'we would love to know if you are in' replaced with 'are you in?' to avoid reintroducing the competitor phrase the editor removed.
payload.gate_note: Weighted enquiry likelihood 1.9 (below 3.8) and 3 must-fix items. Not 'stop': every reader kept reading, clarity 4.7, and the piece meets the brief. Low enquiry is structural for a late-stage how-to whose brief goal is one closing line; the edits address what is fixable in copy. Apply all 10 edits in edit_order to produce 08-final.md.

edits.where: Reminding guests for a destination wedding, Advisor paragraph before the secondary CTA
edits.old: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as one point of contact from start to finish, working in your time zone.
edits.new: When the events your guests are replying to run across a whole weekend, a Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments as one point of contact from start to finish, working in your time zone.
edits.why: Must fix (planner_couple medium, sceptic medium, uhnw medium): the line read as a generic end-to-end ad break with no tie to the section. Now opens on the multi-event weekend the section is about. Only brand-facts claims (venue, travel, vendors and payments; one point of contact start to finish; works in the couple's time zone). No fee, scale, security or guest-chasing claim. Secondary CTA sentence and link untouched.

edits.where: Who to remind and how to reach them, paragraph 2
edits.old: Split the list between families. Each partner, or each set of parents, takes their own side, so every reminder comes from a familiar voice.
edits.new: Split the list between families. Each partner, or each set of parents, takes their own side, so every reminder comes from a familiar voice. Ask each helper to pass every answer back to you as it comes in, so your one guest list stays accurate.
edits.why: Must fix (funding_parent, planner_couple, uhnw all objected to this paragraph): parents asked how answers get back to the couple. Ties the split to the 'Keep one list' section. Says nothing about Wedded Wonderland doing the chasing.

Planner's suggested 'we would love to know if you are in' rejected because it echoes a competitor phrase the editor removed.

edits.new: Once the replies are in, the details firm up: where everyone stays
edits.why: Should fix (planner_couple, sceptic): 'the real planning begins' is a brochure line and wrongly implies stays are arranged only after replies. Primary persona's wording used. Closing CTA untouched.

edits.old: and we will stop politely nagging.
edits.new: and we will set a place for you.
edits.why: Should fix (funding_parent, uhnw turn-offs): 'politely nagging' is the most eager line on the page. Stays light, loses the self-deprecating nag.

edits.new: Keep your list somewhere you trust, share it only with the people helping you, and ask them not to forward or screenshot it.

edits.new: and the travel and accommodation details are at [RSVP web address]. Please also tell us about any dietary, mobility or access needs so we can plan around them.
edits.why: Consider (funding_parent, medium): the destination reminder is the one that matters for older guests before they book travel, and it was the only longer reminder not asking about access needs. Matches the formal email.

edits.where: Keep one list so you only remind the right guests, paragraph 2
edits.old: Nothing sours goodwill faster than reminding someone who has already answered.
edits.new: Reminding someone who has already answered can quickly sour goodwill.

edits.old: Split the list so each side's parents or a trusted sibling contacts
edits.new: Split the list so each side's parents, a trusted sibling or a family assistant contacts
edits.why: Consider (uhnw): some families send reminders through an assistant. Says nothing about what Wedded Wonderland does.

After edits: primary, secondary and closing Concierge UTM links once each with anchor 'Wedded Concierge'; /magazine magnet kept; no CTA deleted or moved
New text has no day/week counts or intervals, prices, statistics, 'best', 'free', 'often', 'usually', 'many', vendor names, em dashes; Australian English

Advisor wording only from brand-facts 'Claims we can make'; nothing on fees, ground team, phone, named person, room blocks, Privileges, scale, security, or the Advisor chasing guests or handling RSVPs
Wonderland Studio wording unchanged; no competitor phrases reintroduced
